headline: Atlassian's AI agent resolutions to cost $1 each from Dec 2026
summary: New pricing for Atlassian's Customer Service Management AI agent will charge $1 per resolution starting December 3, 2026, with no free tier or allowance.
details: Atlassian is set to implement a new pricing model for its Customer Service Management (CSM) AI agent, charging $1.00 for each resolution starting December 3, 2026. This new policy applies from the very first resolution, with no allowances provided on any plan.

This change has caused concern among users, with one customer noting that any attempt to benchmark the AI's performance would require testing in a production environment. The core AI agent functionality itself is included at no extra cost with Service Collection, but the per-resolution charge is specifically for the CSM AI agent.

For those using Jira Service Management (JSM) instead of CSM, the billing structure differs. JSM's AI agents are metered using Rovo credits or assisted conversations, not the per-resolution fee. This distinction is crucial as CSM is Atlassian's app specifically designed for external customer support.

Atlassian is transitioning most JSM customers to its Service Collection bundle during their renewal periods. While CSM is included in Service Collection Standard and Premium plans, the new per-resolution charge applies only to the CSM AI agent, meaning users not employing this specific feature will see no change.

The pricing details and usage documentation explicitly tie the $1 resolution meter to the Customer Service Management AI agent. Unlike other features within Service Collection, there is no included allowance for these AI agent resolutions, meaning costs can escalate quickly based on usage.

Jira Service Management also offers an older 'virtual service agent' which has been metered since October 2024. Service Collection Premium and Enterprise plans include 1,000 assisted conversations monthly, with additional conversations billed at $0.30 each. This meter counts any conversation matched to an intent, including abandoned chats.
